history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: the temple is at Bagodar, not Giridih town - documented with the corrected town. Harihar Dham is famous for its 65-ft (20 m) open-air Shivalinga, claimed as one of the tallest in the world, on a 25-acre complex by the Jamunia river at Bagodar. Jharkhand Tourism states the temple was constructed in 1987 by Pandit Amarnath Mukhopadhyay (late Chief Justice, Calcutta High Court), with a Radha-Krishna temple and a marriage hall added later within the premises. CONFLICT (verify): other sources (e.g. placeguider) say construction started in 1990 and took ~30 years, with the temple trust formed in 1996. Smaller shrines for Parvati, Ganesha, Hanuman and Vishnu stand in the complex. It is a major Sawan/Shravan Poornima pilgrimage and a popular Hindu wedding venue.

name: Harihar Dham, Bagodar
town: Bagodar (CSV town 'Giridih' is WRONG - the temple is at Bagodar, ~60 km southwest of Giridih town)
town_description: Bagodar is a town and block headquarters in Giridih district, Jharkhand, on the Hazaribagh-Bagodar road (NH 100) with the Grand Trunk Road passing close by. It lies about 60 km southwest of the Giridih district headquarters, and Hazaribagh Road railway station is roughly 13 km away. The Jamunia river flows near the town, and the Harihar Dham complex sits by it.

travel.airport: Birsa Munda Airport, Ranchi - about 105 km (verify).
travel.railway: Hazaribagh Road station - about 13 km (per Jharkhand Tourism).
travel.road: On the Hazaribagh-Bagodar road (NH 100); easily reached by buses from Hazaribagh, Vishnugarh, Giridih and Deoghar.

visitor_information.best_time: Sawan month (July-August) and Maha Shivaratri; October-February is the most comfortable season (verify).
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:00 AM - 8:00 PM daily (verify - hours from a place listing, not officially published).
